issues.body: `claims_about_the_route()` returns `sorted(set(found))`, so the `render_alert` assertion sees `["can write to"]` whether that phrase occurs once or many times. Appending a second ALERT_TOKEN-scoped `can write to` sentence inside `render_alert` therefore leaves both the phrase assertion and the independent scoping-clause assertion green, despite the test's explicit contract that a second occurrence must red. This is the duplicated-guard/multiplicity case the added prose says it prevents, so the exact-one claim is not actually tested.
issues.fix_hint: For the separately scanned `render_alert` span, retain occurrence counts (or independently count ALERT_TOKEN-scoped matches) and assert exactly one total match, exactly one `can write to` match, and no other phrasing. Add a non-vacuity fixture containing the same scoped phrase twice and assert that the exact-one predicate rejects it. Keep deduplication only where set membership is the intended property.
issues.title: Maintainer-hint census cannot detect duplicate expected phrases

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The new contract checks are generally careful, but the `pat-validity.py` maintainer-hint census does not enforce the exact-one-occurrence property it claims. Because the detector deduplicates matches, duplicated copies of the expected capability phrase survive the self-test. That leaves the prose guard materially weaker than its stated, load-bearing contract and makes the test non-vacuous for presence but vacuous for multiplicity.
